pull_request.title: Reuse principal-point offsets in EPnP matrix construction
pull_request.body:
## Problem

EPnP constructs the same principal-point offset once for each of its four control-point columns. That performs eight vector subtractions instead of two and, when the inputs are differentiable, retains separate offset buffers for backward.

## Change

Compute `du = u0 - u` and `dv = v0 - v` once and reuse them across the four blocks. The projective-matrix entries, eigensolver, null-space selection and beta-solving code stay the same.

Fixes #544.

## Measured effect

With points, pixels and intrinsics requiring gradients, the complete public output graph retains **six fewer batch-by-point buffers**. At 65,536 correspondences this saves **1,572,864 bytes in float32** or **3,145,728 bytes in float64**, with refinement enabled or disabled. The metric counts distinct storage referenced by saved tensors in the live autograd graph; it is not process peak memory.

The projective calculation performs **2 rather than 8** `aten::sub` operations. I am not claiming a wall-clock speedup from the noisy shared-host timings.

## Validation

- 26 independent checks build the camera equations separately, compare the selected subspace and its gradients with an SVD reference, and recover actual camera poses across unbatched/multiple-batch-axis inputs, float32/float64 and both refinement modes. All 26 also pass on unchanged main.
- The full suite passes on CPU Torch **2.5.1 and 2.6.0**: **426 passed, 18 skipped** on each.
- On each version, 16 public-call comparisons verify bit-identical null bases and returned poses, tolerance-equivalent gradients for points/pixels/intrinsics, and exactly the expected six-buffer storage reduction.
- [Exact-source validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/pypose/actions/runs/44038162521), production head `ba24afb6b87c6240b950a3b77a18aa4e7edb4094`.

The new pose oracle and controlled public comparisons explicitly configure the existing `gelsd` beta solver. During validation, the default QR solver varied in a near-zero beta coefficient even on unchanged inputs; a signed-zero result can trigger the existing `sign(0)` initialization path and a non-finite pose candidate. Independent repeated traces show identical projective matrices, Gram matrices, eigenpairs and null bases across this patch. Default-solver observations are retained separately, and this PR does not claim general bit-identical default-solver poses or change solver selection.

The novelty check covers all 82 distinct PnP source versions across 135 commits reachable from 343 fetched upstream PR heads and 69 existing account branches. Every version, including the original NumPy implementation and renamed helpers, retains all eight principal-point subtractions.
